public_rationale: Microsoft confirms the rounded $37 billion run rate and more than 20 million paid Copilot seats. The central concentration claim remains unsettled. The later $24.1 billion OpenAI-related revenue disclosure measures realized fiscal-year revenue and includes revenue sharing. Dividing it by the March-quarter run rate would not establish the claimed compute share. The public records reviewed also lack a comparable breakdown of growth sources.
limitations: The headline figures are supported, but that does not support the entire proposition.
The claim's qualified growth attribution is not treated as an absolute exclusion of every other product.
The realized OpenAI revenue context relies on reporting because read_page could not access the SEC filing.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft’s $37 billion in annualized AI run rate (sigh) is mostly taken up by OpenAI’s voracious demands for its :compute, and only ever seems to expand based on OpenAI’s compute demands and the now 20 million lost souls paying for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

mostly taken up by OpenAI’s voracious demands for its :compute
20 million lost souls paying for Microsoft 365 Copilot
our_interpretation: Read 'mostly' as more than half of the AI revenue run rate attributable to compute purchased by OpenAI.
Use Microsoft's fiscal third quarter ended March 31, 2026, the latest reported quarter before the post.
Treat the $37 billion and 20 million figures as rounded descriptions of the reported run rate and paid seats.
Paid seats do not necessarily represent distinct individuals paying personally.
Preserve the qualification 'seems': assess the asserted concentration of growth without converting it into an absolute claim that no other AI product earns revenue.
The run rate is a company-reported measure, not realized annual revenue.
criteria.support_condition: Microsoft confirms the headline figures, and a same-period breakdown shows OpenAI compute contributes more than half of the run rate, with growth predominantly attributable to OpenAI compute and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable breakdown shows OpenAI compute contributes half or less, or demonstrates material growth drivers inconsistent with the asserted concentration. A material error in the headline figures would also contradict that component.
